Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

spare time noun

also in my spare time, free time, odd hours

classical

Cic. Leg. 1.9: subsicīva quaedam tempora incurrunt, quae ego perīre nōn patior (Lewis & Short)
Plin. Ep. 3.15.1: aliquid subsicīvī temporis (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 109: cum tempus subsicīvum mihi est
Traupman 43: aliquid temporis subsicīvī

tempus subsicīvum (tempora subsicīva)

subsicīvus, subsicīva, subsicīvum, adjective, with tempus, temporis n.

spare time, odd hours left over from work

A land surveyor’s word: subsicīvum is the strip left over when fields are divided, and so the hours left over from business.

Other words

  • tempus līberum

    also used · modern · Traupman 41, 52

    Classically līberum tempus is time free of obligation (Lewis & Short); the phrase is Traupman’s everyday “free time”.

Examples

  • quantumque ā tuendā rē familiārī prōcūrandōque cultū līberōrum meōrum dabitur ōtium, ea omnia subsicīva et subsecundāria tempora ad colligendās hujuscemodī memoriārum dēlectātiunculās cōnferam

    whatever leisure is left me from managing my household and seeing to my children’s education, all that spare time I shall give to collecting little pleasures of this kind for rememberingGell. praef. 23

See also available, peace.
